purpose: Extend the supported standing-variation filter to trait-specific mutation supply, mutational effect size and pleiotropic coupling while keeping the ecological Model 3 operator unchanged.
biological_question: When standing variation is similarly depleted, can differences in mutational accessibility and pleiotropic coupling alone determine which syndrome components appear first, lag, or evolve together?
primary_endpoints: time to first sustained 0.05 change in access
time to first sustained 0.05 change in investment
fraction of trajectories with only one trait crossing threshold
predeclared_predictions: Under investment_accessible mutation supply, investment reaches its response threshold earlier than access more often than under equal mutation supply.
Under access_accessible mutation supply, access reaches its response threshold earlier than investment more often than under equal mutation supply.
Positive mutational pleiotropy increases coordinated two-trait responses relative to independent mutation.

The sign of ecological selection remains determined by the unchanged Model 3 reproductive operator; mutation accessibility changes realization speed and completeness rather than redefining the ecological optimum.
scientific_role: Test whether syndrome-like coordination or decoupling can emerge from the genetic accessibility layer after ecological routes have been separated.
claim_boundary: Mutation rates and effect sizes are synthetic accessibility contrasts, not natural estimates.
No claim that colour corresponds exactly to investment or morphology exactly to access.
No universal claim that pigmentation is genetically simple or architecture genetically complex.
Pleiotropy parameter is a generic mutational covariance, not a mapped molecular network.
Any literal anthocyanin, corolla-tube or developmental-pathway interpretation requires external genetic evidence.
